Colouring division far east within state shows order. layouts keep Perth west Western Australia Brisbane east Queensland, hierarchy layout keeps outback Queensland’s west.  measure order, compare rank division west east (south north) map rank hexagons state. rank correlation 1 means every division order: Across whole map, hierarchy diffusion layouts move regions distance map. hierarchy layout keeps regions order within groups, diffusion layout keeps outline.
code: order_kept <- function(hex) {   map <- st_coordinates(st_point_on_surface(st_geometry(election)))   tile <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(hex)))   states <- split(seq_len(nrow(map)), election$state)   states <- states[lengths(states) >= 4]   mean(sapply(states, function(i) {     cor(map[i, ], tile[i, ], method = "spearman")[c(1, 4)]   })) } sapply(list(hierarchy = hierarchy, diffusion = diffusion,             compact = compact, slice = slice), order_kept) #> hierarchy diffusion   compact     slice  #> 0.8392524 0.7638197 0.8514918 0.7501734

title: Convert a Map into a Hexagon Tile Map
text: Labor won 94 150 seats 2025 Australian federal election. geographic map result looks like Coalition win, large rural divisions hide Labor’s many small city seats. cartogram equal areas division shows number seats, distorts map beyond recognition. hexagon grid made geogrid gives division space, doesn’t keep states together. hexmap keeps state together, place neighbours.  hexmap includes results aus_election_2025: simplified boundaries division Australian Bureau Statistics, state party won Australian Electoral Commission, licensed CC 4.0. maps made Australian Albers equal-area projection, minor parties combined: method gives every division area:  Colouring divisions state shows difference. geogrid scatters divisions state across grid, four Tasmania’s five seats end mainland. hexmap keeps state one piece, touching states map.  code plots (ggplot2 patchwork) README.Rmd.
code: library(sf) library(hexmap)  party <- c(ALP = "Labor", LP = "Coalition", LNP = "Coalition", NP = "Coalition",            GRN = "Greens") election <- st_transform(aus_election_2025, 3577) election$party <- ifelse(election$party %in% names(party), party[election$party], "Other") library(cartogram) library(geogrid)  # Cartogram election$seats <- 1 election_cartogram <- cartogram_cont(election, "seats", itermax = 20)  # geogrid grid <- calculate_grid(election, grid_type = "hexagonal", seed = 1) election_geogrid <- assign_polygons(election, grid)  # hexmap election_hexmap <- hexmap(election, group = state)

title: Layouts of hexagons — layouts
code: library(sf) # The 2025 Australian federal election, in Australian Albers election <- st_transform(aus_election_2025, 3577)  # Compact blocks, with the ACT on the east side of NSW nsw <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(election[election$state == "NSW", ]))) anchor <- data.frame(group = "ACT", x = nsw[1] + 5e5, y = nsw[2]) election_hex <- hexmap(election, group = state,                        layout = layout_compact(anchor = anchor))  # \donttest{ # The other layouts take a few seconds each # Each state keeps its shape, at the expense of the outline of Australia election_hex <- hexmap(election, group = state,                        layout = layout_hierarchy()) # Keep more of the outline of Australia election_hex <- hexmap(election, group = state,                        layout = layout_diffusion(cartogram = 0.5)) # Compact blocks that touch as the states do election_hex <- hexmap(election, group = state,                        layout = layout_repair(layout_compact())) # }
